resources.string: Forwards ports on this device to a tailcat server over WireGuard, and can run a SOCKS5 proxy through it — no VPN, no Tailscale account. Point an app at http://127.0.0.1:<port>, or at the proxy. On the other machine, tailcat serve <port> prints the address to add here; tailcat serve exit-node lets the proxy reach any address. Several connections run at once, one per server.
Run tailcat serve <port> on the machine you want to reach, then add the address it prints.
The tc… address the server printed
The server\'s port, e.g. 8080; local:remote to listen on another port here (18080:8080). Separate several with commas.

Optional: a SOCKS5 proxy on 127.0.0.1 that goes through the server. server.tailcat:<port> reaches a port on the server; any other address goes out through it when the server runs tailcat serve exit-node. Names resolve on this device. It gets its own login and password; tapping its tag copies the address with them.
No answer: the server is off or does not allow this key
Without one, anyone holding a server\'s address can connect. Start each server with tailcat serve --allow=<this key> to let only this device in; the one key serves every connection.
No key yet: connections use a throwaway identity.
A new key replaces this one. Servers that allow only the old key will refuse this device until you update their --allow.

Lets tailcat clients reach ports on this phone, or go out to the internet through its network — no Tailscale account on either side. They need its address; with a list of client keys, only those get in. It comes up with TailSocks when it was on.
A new address replaces this one. Clients that have the old one will no longer reach this phone.
Nothing to serve: add a port or turn on the exit node
Ports on this phone that clients reach, e.g. 5555 for adb. Separate several with commas.
Clients may go to any address through this phone\'s network — with tailcat socks, or a SOCKS5 port in TailSocks. Their traffic leaves from this phone\'s IP.
nodekey:…, one per line. tailcat genkey --client prints one; another TailSocks shows its key on this screen.
Let in anyone with the address
Without a key list, whoever learns the address gets this phone\'s ports, and its network when it is an exit node.
